questions.explain: The risk scorer is trained on retrospective incident data with a binary target: 1 when an incident started within two hours after the 5-minute feature window, 0 otherwise.
options: 1 if a production incident started within the next two hours of the 5-minute window, else 0
1 if CPU exceeded 80 percent in the window, else 0
1 if the window contained any anomaly, else 0
1 if the DBA was paged during the window, else 0
questions.q: How is the training label defined for the gradient-boosted risk scoring classifier?

questions.explain: The chapter stresses that gap=24 (24 x 5min = 2hr) prevents leakage and that TimeSeriesSplit respects temporal ordering — plain KFold would leak future incident labels into training folds.
options: To speed up cross-validation
To match the 24-hour seasonality cycle
To prevent temporal leakage — 24 five-minute windows equals the 2-hour prediction horizon, so future information cannot leak into training folds
Because KFold is unavailable in scikit-learn
questions.q: Why does the chapter train the risk scorer with TimeSeriesSplit using a gap of 24?

questions.explain: With incidents rare relative to normal windows, accuracy is misleading; average precision penalizes missed detections against normal background exactly the way production alerting requires.
options: Accuracy, because it is the industry standard

Average precision — a model predicting 'no incident' for every window achieves 98%+ accuracy but is operationally useless; average precision penalizes missed detections against a background of normal periods
RMSE, because risk scores are continuous
R-squared, because incidents are seasonal
questions.q: Which evaluation metric does the chapter call the right one for the heavily imbalanced incident dataset, and why?

questions.explain: The LLM-augmented diagnosis pattern is retrieval-augmented generation: incident post-mortem embeddings live in SQL Server 2025's VECTOR column with a DiskANN index, and VECTOR_SEARCH with METRIC='cosine', TOP_N=5 retrieves the most relevant historical context at alert time.
options: Storing query execution plans
Storing DMV snapshots
Storing raw metrics
Storing embeddings of past incident post-mortems so VECTOR_SEARCH can retrieve the top-N semantically similar historical incidents by cosine distance for RAG
questions.q: What role does SQL Server 2025's native VECTOR type with a DiskANN index play in the chapter's architecture?

questions.explain: Killing an idle-in-transaction blocking session is Tier 1 (auto-execute, near-zero blast radius), but dry-run-as-default is non-optional, and the remediation_audit table is INSERT-only to preserve a tamper-evident record.
options: Tier 1 (auto-execute, near-zero risk) — but the remediation procedure must default to dry-run mode so nothing executes without explicit enablement, and every action is written to a write-only audit table
Tier 3, auto-recommend only
Tier 2, but execution happens without human approval
No tier — automated remediation is never permitted
questions.q: A runaway session is blocking others while idle in a transaction. Which remediation tier applies, and what safety default does the chapter require?
